intro: Outlook for investor relations officers on Mac runs in two versions, New Outlook and Legacy Outlook. Use New Outlook. SMU IT says Legacy Outlook was set to stop working on October 1, 2026, and that date has passed. This guide covers the settings, templates, rules and calendar options that matter for IR work, plus how Lazur helps by voice while you work.
tldr: Use New Outlook. SMU IT says Legacy Outlook was set to stop working on October 1, 2026.
Built-in templates need Microsoft 365 and Outlook for Mac 15.35 or later. My Templates does not work in shared mailboxes.
Route analyst and media mail with rules, and sort follow-ups by Flag Due Date.
Lazur points, guides, drafts and dictates by voice. It does not click buttons or operate Outlook for you.

blocks.text: Check which Outlook you are running

Start with the version, because the steps in this guide depend on it. Open Outlook and choose Outlook > About Outlook. Write down the version number, such as 16.114. Microsoft lists new features by version, so that number tells you what your Mac can do.

Next, find the switch between the two versions. SMU IT says the Legacy Outlook toggle sits at the top right of the window. A Microsoft Q&A answer points to Outlook > Legacy Outlook or Help > Legacy Outlook instead. Check both places before you assume it is missing.

A few things matter for IR work. Your license decides whether built-in templates work at all. Your mailbox type decides whether My Templates works. Your signature decides how every outgoing reply looks. Check each one before you plan your week around it.

items: Outlook > About Outlook: note the version number.
Microsoft 365: confirm your account includes it, since built-in templates need it.
Shared IR mailbox: confirm it opens in your sidebar before you rely on it.
Signature: send a test reply to yourself and read the line breaks.

blocks.text: Do this before an earnings week starts. A surprise on results day costs far more than a quiet afternoon spent now.
Set up a shared IR inbox that does not bury you

Many IR teams work from one address that analysts, media and shareholders already use. Add that address as a shared mailbox, so replies go out under the shared address and not one person's name. Full steps are in [how to add a shared mailbox in Outlook](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook).

One catch matters here. Microsoft says the My Templates add-in does not work in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. It also says an administrator may have disabled add-ins, which would hide My Templates. Plan for both cases before the next earnings week.
Keep master drafts in a shared document that the whole team can open. Copy a draft into a message when you need it. That works in any mailbox, and it survives a change of Mac.

blocks.text: Templates for the replies you write every week
Templates earn their keep when the wording stays the same. A holding reply to an analyst who asks for guidance is a good example. So is a note that declines a meeting during a quiet period.

Built-in templates use File > Save As Template to save and File > New > Mail From Template to use. They need a Microsoft 365 subscription and Outlook for Mac 15.35 (170610) or later. Microsoft's article shows no last-updated date, so confirm the steps on your own build.
Build a template step by step

items: Write the email once, in plain words. Read it as if an analyst will see it.
Replace each name, date and figure with a bracketed placeholder, such as [CALL DATE].
Choose File > Save As Template and name it by topic, such as Analyst call request.
Next time, choose File > New > Mail From Template and pick the topic.
Fill every bracket, then read the email again before you send it.

blocks.text: The common mistake is a template with last quarter's figure still in it. Brackets force you to fill every value, so stale numbers stand out. Read the email again before you send it.

Anything that touches disclosure wording should go past your legal or disclosure team before you save it as a template. Lazur can help you find the words and tighten the sentences. It does not know your disclosure policy, and it does not check your figures.
Rules and folders that route analyst and media mail

A rule moves mail before you see it. That helps when one stream, such as media requests, floods the inbox on results day. Full steps are in [how to create a rule in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-rule-in-outlook).

Here is a worked example. Say media requests arrive with the words Media inquiry in the subject line. Create a rule that looks for those words and moves matches to a folder named Media. Check that folder before each call. Your main inbox stays clear.

Watch for false matches. A subject word such as earnings can catch internal chat about earnings. Test the rule against a week of old mail before you trust it. Read what it catches, not just what it moves.

Keep the rule list short. A long list hides mail from the people who need it, and nobody remembers why each rule exists. Put one folder behind each stream. You can make folders with [how to create a folder in Outlook](/how-to/create-a-folder-in-outlook).
Flags and search for follow-ups you cannot lose

Flags work when you use only a few. Flag any message that needs an answer, and clear the flag once you reply. Since version 16.106 (Feb 10, 2026), Mail can sort by Flag Status, Flag Start Date and Flag Due Date.

Sort by Flag Due Date to see what is late. Then use search filters to pull up every thread with one analyst or one fund. Steps are in [how to search with filters in Outlook](/how-to/search-with-filters-in-outlook).
The common mistake is flagging everything. When every message has a flag, no message stands out. Give each flag a due date, even a rough one, so the sort has something to work with.
Calendar options for earnings week

Earnings weeks fill with holds, dial-ins and board slots. Version 16.113 (Sep 16, 2026) added choices that help you manage that load. You can decide whether accepted invitations leave the Inbox. You can decide whether conflicts are declined automatically.

The same release added work-hours and work-location scheduling in Calendar. Set your working hours before you accept a slot in another time zone. Then the slots you see match the hours you can actually work.

Version 16.114 (Oct 14, 2026) lets calendar events use a supported third-party online meeting provider. I did not verify which providers count as supported, so check your Calendar settings before you rely on one.

For invites, see [how to send a meeting invite in Outlook](/how-to/send-a-meeting-invite-in-outlook). To let an assistant or colleague see your schedule, see [how to share your calendar in Outlook](/how-to/share-your-calendar-in-outlook).
Keep the call calendar open beside your inbox. Version 16.113 lets you open Mail, Calendar or People in a separate window. A second screen works well for call prep during earnings week.
Edit a message in the Outbox before it leaves
Version 16.111 (Jul 14, 2026) lets you edit messages held in the Outbox before they send. Open the held message, fix the line, and let it go. That matters when a figure in an outgoing note is wrong.
For a longer safety net, use Schedule send or Undo Send. The steps for both are in [how to delay delivery of an email in Outlook](/how-to/delay-delivery-of-an-email-in-outlook).
Do not count on any single safety net. Read every number and name before you press send. Treat the Outbox as the backup, not the plan.
Legacy Outlook is ending, so plan the switch

SMU IT says Legacy Outlook for Mac was set to stop working on October 1, 2026. The reason is that Microsoft is retiring the connection protocol used to reach Exchange Online. That date has passed. If your Mac still runs Legacy Outlook, ask your IT team before you change anything.

I could not confirm that date on a Microsoft page. A Microsoft Q&A answer gives the same reason, but it is AI-generated and carries a disclaimer. Treat the date as a strong lead to check, not a settled fact.
Sources also disagree on local On My Computer folders. One blog says they do not carry over. Another says they do. Back up before you switch. A full Time Machine backup is the simplest safety net.
Before you switch to New Outlook

items: Copy each signature into a note. SMU IT says line breaks may change after the switch.
Recreate saved searches as Smart Folders, as SMU IT advises.
Let local folder data finish migrating before you delete anything.
Test each rule again after the switch, and fix any that no longer work.
Use native PST import, added in 16.110 (Jun 16, 2026), for older archives.

blocks.text: Microsoft's Q&A thread also says Outlook 2024 does not support Legacy Outlook. If you run Outlook 2024, the switch is a different job, so check your version first.
What to say to Lazur while you work in Outlook

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘, which is Option plus Command, and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. If you ask where a button is, it draws a circle and a label around it.
When you ask how to do something, Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. You do the clicking, so you stay in control of your mail.
Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook or any other app. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. Think of it as a sharp colleague who sits beside you and points.
Dictation and drafts for IR notes

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets hold lines you repeat, such as a standard disclaimer. The personal dictionary holds names that speech tools often get wrong, such as fund names and analyst firms.
Clipboard slots keep pieces of text ready for the next message. That is handy when you copy a figure from a PDF and need it in several emails.

Drafting is one of the best uses of Lazur for IR mail. Ask for a holding reply, then read every line. Lazur does not check your figures against filings, and it does not know what you may say before results.
Mistakes IR officers make with Outlook on Mac

items: Staying on Legacy Outlook past its end date instead of asking IT what to do.
Saving a template with last quarter's figure still in it.
Expecting My Templates to work in a shared IR mailbox.
Writing a rule keyword that also catches internal chat.
Flagging every message, so the flags stop meaning anything.
Switching versions without checking signatures and saved searches first.

blocks.text: Most of these come from doing the setup in a hurry. A slow hour in a quiet week saves a bad morning on results day.
How heavy the IR workload really is

NIRI's 2024 career survey ran from May to July 2024. It drew 429 responses from about 3,000 corporate practitioners. Nearly 80% of IR respondents manage responsibilities beyond IR, up from 62% in 2022.
The survey also found that 20% of respondents handle competitive intelligence and 20% handle ESG or sustainability. Those duties add mail to the same inbox that carries analyst requests.
No public source I found measures how much email an IR officer handles. Treat email as one part of a heavy week, not the whole week.
One secondary blog says heads of IR average 52 to 60 hours a week. Its sample size conflicts with NIRI's, so use that figure as a rough guess only.
A short setup for this week

items: Confirm your version with Outlook > About Outlook.
Add the IR inbox as a shared mailbox, if you have not already.
Save your most repeated replies as templates, with brackets for every figure.
Build one rule for your busiest stream, then test it on old mail.
Set a due date on every open flag.
Back up before any switch, and check the Legacy Outlook notes above.

blocks.text: When the list is done, ask Lazur to walk you through the next step. Hold ⌥⌘ and say what you are stuck on. Lazur circles the control and guides you from there.
Privacy and pricing

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked stays on your Mac.

There is a free trial with no credit card, and dictation is unlimited on both paid plans. Check [pricing](/pricing) for current plan details. You can start with the [download page](/download), or read more on the [investor relations page](/for/investor-relations-officers).

faq.question: Which Outlook should investor relations officers use on Mac in 2026?
faq.answer: Use New Outlook. SMU IT says Legacy Outlook was set to stop working on October 1, 2026, and that date has passed. Microsoft's Q&A thread gives a similar reason, though its answer is AI-generated, so check your own Mac first.

faq.question: Do Outlook templates work in a shared IR mailbox?
faq.answer: Microsoft says the My Templates add-in does not work in shared mailboxes opened in Outlook for Mac. Built-in templates use File > Save As Template and File > New > Mail From Template, and need Microsoft 365 and version 15.35 or later. Microsoft's pages do not say built-in templates work in shared mailboxes, so test one first.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Outlook?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Outlook. Hold ⌥⌘ in Outlook and ask a question, and Lazur answers out loud and points at things on screen. It does not click buttons or operate Outlook for you.

faq.question: Can Lazur draft investor replies?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask for a draft and Lazur types it for you to read. Check every number, date and disclosure line yourself before you send. Lazur does not check your figures against filings.

faq.question: How do I check my Outlook version on Mac?
faq.answer: Choose Outlook > About Outlook and note the version number, such as 16.114. Microsoft lists new features by version in its release notes, so that number tells you what your build can do.

faq.question: How many IR officers have duties beyond IR?
faq.answer: NIRI's 2024 survey found nearly 80% of IR respondents manage responsibilities in addition to IR, up from 62% in 2022. The survey drew 429 responses from about 3,000 practitioners. It does not measure email time.

faq.question: Is there a Lazur trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur has a free trial with no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app. Current plan details are on the pricing page. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans.
